ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION:  
FIND: Per-model `monotonic_decline` is remediated as a global pathology. The detector emits a model-specific diagnosis with `evidence["model_id"]` at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3119), but the chain uses the all-model transform at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5998), and `apply_diagnosis()` stores state under one shared `_remediation_state["monotonic_decline"]` at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L6229) and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L6372). Read-only repro: a decline diagnosis for `m1` added directives to both `m1` and `m2`, then a later `m2` decline saw the same shared state and no new fix. One model’s local decline can therefore contaminate every model’s directives and remediation progress.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
FIX:

FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION:  
FIND: Failed rounds are being fed into the analytical decline detector as if they were genuine low-yield rounds. `record_model_round()` always appends `finding_count` to `_model_finding_history` at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3029), then `monotonic_decline` runs over that history at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3110). Read-only repro: `8 -> 4 -> 0` with the last round marked `failed=True` emits `monotonic_decline` for `[8, 4, 0]`. That confuses transport/protocol failure with analytical exhaustion and can trigger the wrong immune chain.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
FIX:
```text
<<<<
self._model_finding_history[model_id].append(finding_count)
...
self._model_response_times[model_id].append(response_time)
...
self._model_response_chars[model_id].append(response_chars)
====
if not failed:
    self._model_finding_history[model_id].append(finding_count)
    self._model_response_times[model_id].append(response_time)
    self._model_response_chars[model_id].append(response_chars)
>>>>
```
FOLLOW: This keeps `monotonic_decline`, CPF, and `_identify_worst_performers()` on analytical data only. Failure pressure still flows through `_model_failure_counts`, so failure handling remains intact instead of being double-counted as “decline.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION:  
FIND: The “verification miscalibration” detector is wired to the wrong input. `Finding.verified` is documented as independent verification at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L367), but `process_round()` uses it to build per-model “self-verification” rates at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5538), and `record_model_verification_rate()` explicitly says “self-verification rate” at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L6526). That means the detector is not measuring self-calibration at all; it is measuring externally verified yield and then prescribing self-verification fixes.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
FIX:
```text
<<<<
verified: bool = False  # Whether finding was independently verified (SymPy, etc.)
====
verified: bool = False  # Whether finding was independently verified (SymPy, etc.)
self_verified: Optional[bool] = None  # Model's own VERIFIED judgment, if present
>>>>

<<<<
for f in findings:
    _vr_by_model[f.model_id].append(f.verified)
====
for f in findings:
    if f.self_verified is not None:
        _vr_by_model[f.model_id].append(float(f.self_verified))
>>>>

<<<<
"""Record a model's self-verification rate for this round."""
====
"""Record a model's self-reported verification rate for this round."""
>>>>
```
FOLLOW: The finding extractor/parser must now populate `self_verified`; until it does, this detector should stay silent rather than mislabel low external accuracy as self-verification miscalibration. The diagnosis text and remediation rationale then become truthful without changing the rest of the branch.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION:  
FIND: The real-time manager interface emits failure events but not recovery decisions. `ManagerEventType` declares recovery events at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5001), but `get_recovery()` never calls `_emit_event()` at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4596). Read-only repro: a timeout followed by recovery produced event stream `['TIMEOUT']`, with no `RETRY` event. That leaves PM-side monitoring blind to what the manager actually decided to do.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
FIX:
```text
<<<<
self._record_failure(model_id, round_idx, failure_type, action)

# Execute exclusion if needed
if action == RecoveryAction.EXCLUDE:
====
self._record_failure(model_id, round_idx, failure_type, action)

recovery_event_type = {
    RecoveryAction.RETRY: ManagerEventType.RETRY,
    RecoveryAction.RETRY_EXTENDED: ManagerEventType.RETRY,
    RecoveryAction.RETRY_CLARIFIED: ManagerEventType.RETRY,
    RecoveryAction.REALLOCATE: ManagerEventType.REALLOCATE,
    RecoveryAction.EXCLUDE: ManagerEventType.EXCLUDE,
    RecoveryAction.ABORT: ManagerEventType.ABORT,
}.get(action)
if recovery_event_type is not None:
    self._emit_event(
        ManagerEvent(
            event_type=recovery_event_type,
            model_id=model_id,
            round_idx=round_idx,
            detail=f"{failure_type.name} -> {action.value}",
            metadata={"failure_type": failure_type.name, "recovery_action": action.value},
        )
    )

# Execute exclusion if needed
if action == RecoveryAction.EXCLUDE:
>>>>
```
FOLLOW: Event consumers will now see both the failure and the chosen recovery path in real time. `RoundResult.recovery_actions` can stay as-is; this fix just makes the event stream consistent with the class contract.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
